Chapter 3: The Reach of Grace—No One Is Beyond Hope.
You know, it’s so easy to start thinking that some mistakes are just too big to forgive. Regret can settle in, almost like a heavy fog, and suddenly you’re convinced that your past has completely ruled out any chance for a fresh start.
Ever find yourself replaying those stories in your mind—broken promises, things you wish you hadn’t said, opportunities you let slip away? It can feel like there’s this wall you just can’t get through.
Let me tell you about a man who carried that weight for years. He’d made choices that hurt the people he loved most. No matter how hard he tried to make things right, the past just clung to him, like a shadow that wouldn’t let go. He started to wonder—was there really any hope left, or was he just too far gone?
But here’s where grace steps in.
Grace has this incredible way of reaching into even the darkest corners of our lives. It doesn’t avoid brokenness or run from failure. No, it moves toward the people who feel the most unworthy—offering a fresh start, right when it seems impossible.
Picture this: a group of people gathered, each carrying their own story of regret. Some had betrayed friends. Some had wasted years. Others had just given up hope. They expected to be judged, maybe even punished. But instead? They found a welcome, a seat at the table, and the promise that their past wouldn’t define their future.
That’s the real scandal of grace. It doesn’t keep score. It never writes anyone off. Grace looks beyond every mistake and sees the person underneath—offering restoration instead of rejection. And for anyone who’s ever been told they’re beyond hope, that’s almost too good to believe.
Yet, again and again, grace proves there’s no one it can’t reach. You’ll find it in prison cells, in hospital rooms, during quiet moments when regret hits hard—or even in those desperate cries for help. Grace shows up in the lowest moments and lifts people up—not because they’ve earned it, but simply because they’re loved.
There’s a quiet strength in knowing that nothing—no failure, no weakness, not even your worst decisions—can separate you from this love. Grace is stubborn. It refuses to let go, even when you try to run from it. It chases after you, forgives you, and pulls you back in.
So, if you’ve spent years thinking you’re too far gone, grace wants to tell you a different story. It invites you to set down your shame and pick up hope. Because your worth? It’s not determined by your past—but by a love that never, ever gives up on you.
